name: Raj Singh
experience: Senior faculty at Shiva Yoga Niketan
bio: Raj leads the daily Hatha and Ashtanga practice at Shiva Yoga Niketan. His classes focus on precise alignment, steady breath and building the strength and discipline that a lifelong practice needs — always taught in the traditional way, step by step.
Outside the shala Raj enjoys early-morning walks along the Ganges and time in the Himalayan foothills, and believes that a calm, simple daily routine is the foundation of every good practice.
education: Traditional yoga training, Rishikesh (to be confirmed)

name: Gokul Bisht
experience: Senior faculty at Shiva Yoga Niketan
bio: Gokul teaches the anatomy and physiology modules of our teacher training courses. He helps students understand how the body moves in each asana, how to practise safely, and how to adapt postures for different bodies and abilities.
His classes connect modern anatomy with traditional yogic knowledge, so that students leave able to teach with both confidence and care.
education: Traditional yoga training, Rishikesh (to be confirmed)

name: Shashank Badoni
experience: Senior faculty at Shiva Yoga Niketan
bio: Shashank joins Shiva Yoga Niketan as guest faculty for yoga philosophy. His lectures explore the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, the Bhagavad Gita and the wider Vedic tradition, and how their teachings apply to modern life.
Known for lively discussion and open questions, he encourages students to think deeply and experience philosophy as a living practice rather than theory.
education: Traditional yoga training, Rishikesh (to be confirmed)

name: Gopal
experience: Senior faculty at Shiva Yoga Niketan
bio: Gopal is a Hatha Yoga master whose teaching draws on the classical texts, including the Hatha Yoga Pradipika. His classes combine asana, pranayama, shatkarma and meditation as one complete, integrated practice.
Patient and grounded, he guides students of every level to find steadiness and ease in their practice.
education: Traditional yoga training, Rishikesh (to be confirmed)

name: Angela Carbone
bio: I enjoy getting to know my students and building meaningful relationships. I understand that each person is unique and that they have diverse cultural backgrounds, so I strive to actively listen and empower them to be an advocate for the health and wellness goals that are important to them. I'm dedicated to providing compassionate and individualized care through patient education and evidence-based yoga therapy.

I find joy by doing almost any outdoor activity, including hiking, running, and exploring with our furbabies. I enjoy spending time with family and friends. I also strive to live mindfully and intentionally by creating uplifting routines and relaxing rituals.
education: University of Virginia, M.D. of Medicine
certification: National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants

name: Meghan Conner
bio: My yoga journey began in my early twenties during a period of significant personal change. Through consistent practice I discovered how much yoga could offer beyond physical flexibility — it became my anchor in mindfulness and self-compassion. I now bring that transformative power to each of my students, guiding them with patience and warmth.

Outside the studio, I love swimming, cooking plant-based meals, and reading. I believe that everything we do off the mat informs our practice, and I encourage my students to cultivate curiosity in every area of their lives.
education: Kripalu School of Yoga & Health, RYT-500

name: Sofia Renner
bio: My practice is rooted in the Iyengar tradition, which emphasises precision, alignment, and the use of props to bring the full benefits of postures to every body. I love working with students of all abilities, adapting my teaching to meet each person exactly where they are — whether beginners or experienced practitioners.

When I am not teaching, you will find me in my garden, practising tai chi at sunrise, or writing about holistic health. I believe that stillness is one of the most radical acts of self-care, and I strive to create that space for every student.
education: BKS Iyengar Yoga Institute, Pune – Certified Teacher
certification: International Yoga Teachers Association – Certified Instructor

name: Lena Hart
bio: I came to yoga through dance, and that background informs the fluid, expressive way I teach. My classes feel more like moving meditations than structured exercise sessions. I want each student to find their own rhythm and trust their body's inner wisdom.

In my free time I choreograph community dance events, paint watercolours, and walk barefoot along the coast whenever I can. Nature is my greatest teacher, and I try to weave its rhythms into every class I lead.
education: Chopra Center for Wellbeing – Primordial Sound Meditation
certification: Yoga Alliance – RYT-500, Prenatal Yoga Certified

name: Maya Tran
bio: Growing up immersed in two cultures taught me how powerful it is to find common ground through shared practices. Yoga gave me that bridge. My teaching draws on classical Hatha roots while integrating modern anatomy and trauma-sensitive principles.

Outside the mat I am passionate about herbalism, sound healing, and community building. I host monthly women's circles and seasonal fire ceremonies that help people reconnect with themselves and each other in deeply meaningful ways.
education: Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centre – Advanced Teachers Training

name: Priya Sharma
bio: My relationship with yoga started at age seven in Chennai, where I studied traditional Ashtanga under my grandmother's guidance. Those early years instilled in me a deep reverence for the practice as a whole life system — not just a physical discipline. I bring that reverence to every class I teach.

I am also a certified Ayurvedic nutrition consultant, and I love integrating dietary and lifestyle wisdom into my teachings. Real transformation happens when we align our bodies, minds, and daily habits with the natural world around us.
education: SVYASA University, Bangalore – Bachelor of Yogic Sciences
certification: Yoga Alliance – E-RYT 500 & Ayurvedic Wellness Counselor

title: Yoga Course For Beginners
tagline: A four-week preparatory yoga series that introduces newcomers to all the basic fundamentals of yoga — asana, pranayama, meditation and philosophy.
cardSummary: A gentle, welcoming introduction to yoga — build a strong foundation in postures, breath, and mindful movement at your own pace.
introTitle: Yoga Course for Beginners in India
introParas: Shiva Yoga Niketan has developed a new yoga system for newcomers. The four-week preparatory yoga series introduces students to all the basic fundamentals of Yoga. In the present time there is a dilemma among most of us — whether yoga knowledge will be helpful, whether we will be able to do meditation, asanas and postures correctly, and whether we will understand the changes happening within the body through yoga. Keeping these questions in mind, Shiva Yoga Niketan has started a special yoga series to develop a deep yoga understanding among all.

In this yoga series students will be told how they can understand the science of life through yoga power and fulfil their living values, so that they can improve their life in a physical, moral and social manner. You will understand the history, yoga philosophy and development of yoga, and analyse the famous yoga literature in depth — discovering the goal of yoga and the practice that can help you fulfil it in your personal and professional life.
learnPoints: During the course, with the help of asanas and different body postures, students will be told about the problems of the human body and their body abilities for better yoga performance.
With the help of right asana and postures, students will be able to understand how they can correct their shortcomings and do things with stability.

By passive stretching techniques, students will feel the energy and flexibility in their health. By applying some simple asanas, students will be able to understand and co-ordinate with the architecture of their nervous system.

With the help of regular pranayama, students will experience energy within. They will also learn the reasons for obstruction in the body's energy, and how those causes can be treated through pranayama.

Meditation power will be developed from regular yoga practice, which is necessary today for everyone. Students will be given the best advice on yoga practice and proper guidance to strengthen their body health.
With the help of philosophical and moral knowledge, students will develop awareness towards different dimensions of life so they can experience inner peace and fulfilment from within.
ethicsPoints: You will know the ancient science given in the Patanjali Yoga Sutras, Hatha Yoga Pradipika, Swara Yoga and Bhagavad Gita.
You will be able to understand the structure of the human body through intense knowledge of pranayama, shatkarma and meditation.
You will understand the development aspects of Vedic principles and personality.
Mantra pronunciation and kirtan will be part of your daily activities.
Changes in yoga techniques according to the personality of the student can be made, so that students benefit more from the practices.
Suitable meals for physical, mental and spiritual development will be included with yoga practices.
To understand the problems of all students, presentations and question & answer sessions will be conducted.
All students should keep in mind that Shiva Yoga Niketan teaches only the traditional principles of Hatha and Raja Yoga.
Behaviour plays an important role in learning and evaluating. Students should understand the rules and community ideas suggested by the ancient sages for yoga practice.
Food prepared at Shiva Yoga Niketan is according to the ancient guidelines of Ayurveda and yoga. All students are expected to adapt their diet habits according to yoga.
All students should reach their class on time; students who do not come on time will not be allowed to attend the classes.
All students are requested to clear their dues before leaving the premises.
Accommodation facility is available with meals during the course, and only vegetarian food will be made available — no non-vegetarian meals will be provided on the premises.
All students should be mentally and physically fit before the beginning of the yoga course; if their health is not good they are advised to consult their doctor.

title: 200 Hrs Hatha Yoga Teacher Training
tagline: A Yoga Alliance (USA) compliant certification rooted in classical Hatha yoga — asana, pranayama, philosophy, anatomy and the art of teaching.
cardSummary: A comprehensive certification rooted in classical Hatha yoga — asana, alignment, philosophy, and the art of teaching.
introParas: Shiva Yoga Niketan runs its 200-hour Hatha Yoga Teacher Training course in compliance with Yoga Alliance (USA) standards. The purpose of running this course is that students can acquire academic knowledge along with primary yoga practice and can choose yoga as a profession. Students are encouraged by the traditional ideas of the progressive patterns of Hatha Yoga so that they can gain a deeper experience of yoga science.

There is a misconception about Hatha Yoga (Hatha Yoga Pradipika) that it has no spiritual goal, which is wrong — spiritual experiences can be achieved through the physiological yoga process of Hatha Yoga. All of us are caught in emotions like anger, greed and attachment; Hatha Yoga makes everyone free from these emotions. Hatha Yoga teaches us to stay steadfast with stability. Yoga means to unite — in Hatha Yoga we fully concentrate the mind at one point and keep the body firm through meditation and postures.
learnTitle: What the 200 Hours of Hatha Yoga Provides
learnPoints: Asana: In the morning, regular 4 hours of yoga exercises from Monday to Sunday, practising therapeutic postures and awakening the important points of the body. All information related to vinyasa will be given so that everyone can learn how to create their own vinyasa sequence.
Pranayama: Through regular pranayama practice you will feel the source of energy within yourself and be able to use that inner energy positively in your life.
Yoga nidra and meditation will also be taught to all students so they can understand the importance of relaxation and meditation with intensity and use it in their life with confidence.

You will learn the principles of Hatha Yoga through yoga postures so you can share your experience with your students and make them aware of the rules, methodology, practices and science of yoga in their class.
Mantras and bhajans will be included with daily yoga exercises so everyone can experience mental peace during the course.

Yoga philosophy includes the study of the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, so that yoga can be used for the prevention of physical and mental disorders. Hatha Yoga Pradipika will be studied to understand the curative aspects of classical Hatha Yoga.
topicsHeading: 200 Hour Hatha Yoga Teacher Training Syllabus

topics.title: Asanas
topics.body: Practice of the yogasanas consists of 4 hours each day from Monday to Saturday. Morning practice focuses on asanas with a therapeutic approach and opening the vital centers of the body. Students also practise the modified vinyasa flow and learn to create their own vinyasa sequences. In the evening practice they are trained in teaching methodology, and from the third week onwards they teach classes for 200-hour level students.

topics.title: Pranayama
topics.body: Practice of yogic pranayama (breath work) every day provides a solid foundation for increasing the pranic reserves within, using it positively to gain vitality at various levels and to be able to teach it skillfully in their classes.

topics.title: Yoga Nidra & Meditation
topics.body: Yoga nidra and meditation are practised regularly to allow students to understand relaxation and meditation more deeply and to use them with confidence in their own teaching classes.

topics.title: Yoga Anatomy
topics.body: Students study the various anatomical and physiological concepts in correlation with the yogic practices, in order to have a deeper experience of in-class explanations, methodology, alignment in positions, demonstration, cues, correction and feedback techniques of teaching.

topics.title: Yoga Philosophy
topics.body: The in-depth study of the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali gives insights into yoga as a preventive medicine for various physical and mental disorders, forming a firm foundation for learning the therapeutic applications of yogic techniques. Hatha Yoga Pradipika is studied to learn the curative aspects of yoga and the correct classical techniques.

topics.title: Mantra & Bhajans
topics.body: Mantra chanting and bhajans add a holistic experience to the course and make students able to use them in their class teachings more effectively.

topics.title: Yoga Therapy & Diet
topics.body: Yoga therapy sessions provide detailed knowledge about pathological conditions related to several common disorders and how yoga can be used to restore health and well-being, along with the importance of a yogic diet suitable from physiological, mental and spiritual perspectives.

title: 200 Hrs Vinyasa Yoga Teacher Training
tagline: A Yoga Alliance (USA) accredited training in the flowing, breath-linked art of Vinyasa — taught through the ancient Gurukul method in Rishikesh, India.
cardSummary: Master the flowing, breath-linked sequences of Vinyasa and learn to guide dynamic, creative classes with confidence.
introTitle: 200 Hour Vinyasa Yoga Teacher Training, Rishikesh India
introParas: Shiva Yoga Niketan's 200-hour Vinyasa Yoga Teacher Training program is accredited by Yoga Alliance (USA). Whether you are a beginner trainee or an experienced practitioner, you can enroll for this training program. Through the ancient Gurukul teaching method you will practise the vinyasa flow on a daily basis and make changes in your thought process by gaining spiritual experiences.

Vinyasa is one of the most prominent contemporary styles of yoga, encompassing many sorts of practice — whether it is Ashtanga or Power Yoga. Vinyasa — also called 'flow' — means to organise something in a special way; for example, to improve the performance of the asanas through practice.

The beginner's version of the vinyasa is Plank → Knees, Chest, Chin → Cobra → Downward-Facing Dog. The advanced version is Plank → Chaturanga Dandasana → Upward-Facing Dog → Downward-Facing Dog. When the instructor says 'go through the vinyasa at your own pace', they mean to do a plank, chaturanga, and upward-facing dog, using your breath to measure when to move on to the next pose.

title: 200 Hrs Kundalini Yoga Teacher Training
tagline: A Yoga Alliance (USA) accredited immersion into the science of Kundalini — awakening the divine energy within through practice, meditation and restraint.
cardSummary: Awaken your energy through kriyas, mantra, and meditation — a transformative training in the yoga of awareness.
introTitle: 200 Hour Kundalini Yoga Teacher Training, Rishikesh India
introParas: The 200-hour teacher training program is accredited by Yoga Alliance (USA). The purpose of running this course is that students can acquire academic knowledge along with primary yoga practice and choose yoga as their profession. Yoga is a process of continuous learning and experience — we want you to walk on the path of Yoga and experience peace and fulfilment in your life. We encourage our students to know the progressive nature of traditional yoga and the science of Kundalini; the aim is not only physical practice, but to improve life by learning the principles of yoga science.

About Kundalini — The Kundalini is a divine power, located like a serpent at the lower point of the body. As long as it stays there, the person continues to run towards worldly subjects; but when it awakens, a spiral wave seems to rise upward — a very divine experience. There are seven chakras in our body: besides the Muladhara, the six Kundalini chakras are Swadhisthana, Manipura, Anahata, Vishuddha, Ajna and Sahasrara.

One end of the Kundalini rests on the Muladhara chakra, while the other is wrapped around the spinal cord; as it moves upward, its purpose is to reach the seventh chakra, Sahasrara. If the person abandons restraint and meditation, this cycle can stop at any chakra. Continuous yoga practice, meditation and restraint can be utilised to awaken the Kundalini, and in our program all the important rules and principles for awakening it will be explained. Kundalini Yoga has had a great influence on the systems of Tantra and the Shakta community.
